newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - July 31.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - July 31.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- President Fidel Ramos welcomes the Supreme Court decision to hear a new petition of People's Initiative for Reform, Modernisation and Action on the ground that the plea to change the Constitution is entirely different from the two petitions it earlier rejected. (ALL PAPERS)
- Two active low pressure areas east of the country have intensified into tropical depressions, the Philipine Atmospheric, Geophyical and Astronomical Services Administration says. (MANILA BULLETIN)
- Senator Ramon Magsaysay says he plans to run for president in next year's election. (PHILIPPINE STAR)
- Education Secretary Ricardo Gloria warns schoolchildren not to bring their Japanese electronic toy to school. (PHILIPPINE DAILY INQUIRER)
- The Philippine peso falls sharply as monetary authorities impose new guidelines to discourage dollar hoarding. (ALL PAPERS)
- Foreign chambers urge the central bank to stop managing the float on the peso. (ALL PAPERS)
- Transportation Secretary Arturo Enrile says construction of the 102-km Manila-Clark Rapid Railway System will start this month. (MANILA BULLETIN)

- Speculative pressure on Asian currencies will ease in the short term and it will not change the overall prospects of the region's economic growth, Robert Denhamn, chairman of Salomon Brothers Inc, says. (BUSINESSWORLD)
